title: Recording: Be Here Now by George Harrison | 1972
content:
Apple Studios, London
Producer: George Harrison
Engineer: Phil McDonald

George Harrison recorded ‘Be Here Now’, for his fourth solo album Living In The Material World, on 12 October 1972.

The basic track had Klaus Voormann’s upright bass on track one, and Jim Keltner’s drums on two and three. Harrison’s acoustic guitar was on track six, and his vocals on 10. Nicky Hopkins’ piano was on tracks seven and eight, and Gary Wright’s harmonium was on nine.

The first two takes were recorded onto the same tape reel used the previous day for recording ‘Don’t Let Me Wait Too Long’.

The song’s arrangement was in place from the beginning, suggesting that rehearsal takes also took place. Take two was considered the best, and became the album master version.

The band continued recording, however, although only takes 11, 14, and 19 were complete. Takes 3-18 were on a second tape reel, which had Wright’s organ on tracks 11 and 12, and take 19 – the final recording of the day – was on a third reel.
